verdict.rationale: Riveter's scrape endpoint converts a single URL to text, so it is not documented as a batch operation. Its enrichment runs can apply web scrapes across input rows, up to 10,000 rows per /enrich request, and execute asynchronously with webhook delivery or polling. That gives an asynchronous, large-batch path, but it goes through AI enrichment rather than a dedicated bulk-scrape API. Missing for 10: a documented batch or async mode for the scrape endpoint itself, explicit confirmation that enrichment rows can be raw URL lists returning scraped text, and independent or hands-on corroboration of throughput at thousands of URLs.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can batch scrape thousands of URLs asynchronously

citations.quote: An enrichment takes rows of input data and fills in new columns using AI, web searches, web scrapes, and other tools.
up to 10,000 rows per `/enrich` request with `enrichment_id`
Pass webhook_url in the JSON body when starting a run and Riveter POSTs the full results to your URL when it finishes
A scrape lets you turn a URL into easily parseable text.
